evals.prompt:
Tenho 2h pra fazer esse teste técnico, me ajuda a começar. Enunciado:

"Desenvolva um sistema para uma pequena biblioteca comunitária. Deve ser possível cadastrar livros (título, autor, ano de publicação e ISBN) e membros (nome e e-mail). O bibliotecário registra empréstimos de livros para membros, com data de devolução prevista, e marca a devolução quando o livro volta. Um livro que já está emprestado não pode ser emprestado novamente até ser devolvido. O sistema deve exibir uma lista dos empréstimos atrasados. Publique a aplicação e envie o link."
evals.expected_output: Plan with livro, membro and emprestimo (fk to both) in the right order, 'book already on loan' rule in the service with a test, overdue as a computed value/screen, assumptions (e.g.: unique ISBN?), steps with commit/push, no code written.
expectations: Doesn't write code or change files; ends waiting for the user's confirmation
Each resource appears as a /new-resource command with typed fields, in fk order (referenced first)
Each business rule in the brief has a place in the back (service/HTTP status) and an associated pytest test
Ambiguities appear as assumptions with an explicit default value
Asks at most 3 blocking questions
Ordered steps with commit/push, including checking the deploy right at the start
Estimates time per step, with MVP within ~100 min and extras separate from the MVP
emprestimo has fk to livro and to membro and comes after both
The 'book already on loan' rule is validated in the back with a 4xx status and covered by a test
Overdue loans are computed in the back (due < today and not returned) or in a dedicated screen/filter
Return is modeled (return date/flag field or a return action)
Step 0 creates the project repo with /new-project and a kebab-case domain name
There is an explicit step to connect the new repo's deploy (Supabase/Render/Vercel) with an estimated time
Removing Task at the end includes updating/replacing Task's E2E tests (tests/app.spec.ts)
Loan has no free editing (no:edit or equivalent) and return is its own action (POST /{id}/devolver or similar)
Deleting a book or member with loans returns 409, with a test

evals.prompt:
vou fazer esse case agora, prazo de 2 horas. o que eu faço primeiro?

"Crie uma aplicação de controle de pedidos para uma loja. Produtos têm nome, preço e quantidade em estoque. Um pedido tem um cliente (nome), uma data e um ou mais itens; cada item é um produto com uma quantidade. O total do pedido deve ser calculado automaticamente. Ao criar um pedido, o estoque dos produtos deve ser reduzido, e não deve ser possível criar um pedido com quantidade maior que o estoque disponível. Diferencial: um dashboard com o total vendido e os produtos mais vendidos."
evals.expected_output: Plan that identifies order item as a resource/table with two fks or nested creation, estimates the extra cost, puts the stock rule in the service with a transaction and a test, total computed in the back, dashboard as an extra, customer as a field (not a resource), no code written.
expectations: Doesn't write code or change files; ends waiting for the user's confirmation
Each resource appears as a /new-resource command with typed fields, in fk order (referenced first)
Each business rule in the brief has a place in the back (service/HTTP status) and an associated pytest test
Ambiguities appear as assumptions with an explicit default value
Asks at most 3 blocking questions
Ordered steps with commit/push, including checking the deploy right at the start
Estimates time per step, with MVP within ~100 min and extras separate from the MVP
Order item is modeled as its own table with fk to order and product (or nested creation) and the plan says this goes beyond a simple /new-resource
Stock validation and reduction happen in the back in a single transaction (all or nothing)
Order total is computed in the back
Customer is a field on the order (name), not a separate resource
Dashboard is treated as an extra/differential, outside the MVP
Step 0 creates the project repo with /new-project and a kebab-case domain name
There is an explicit step to connect the new repo's deploy (Supabase/Render/Vercel) with an estimated time
Removing Task at the end includes updating/replacing Task's E2E tests (tests/app.spec.ts)
Order item is NOT created via /new-resource and has no screen/CRUD of its own: it's a model/schema nested in the order POST
Order is marked without edit/delete (no:edit,delete or an explicit equivalent) because of stock

evals.prompt: Recebi esse enunciado pra entrevista de amanhã, é bem curto: "Faça um app de agendamento para uma barbearia. Clientes podem marcar horário com um barbeiro. Tem que ter login." Tenho 2h. Como eu faço?
evals.expected_output: Plan that recognizes the vague brief, lists assumptions (slot duration, business hours, who logs in), treats login as outside the template with a minimal version and cost, rule against two appointments at the same time/barber in the service with a test, asks at most 3 blocking questions, no code written.
expectations: Doesn't write code or change files; ends waiting for the user's confirmation
Each resource appears as a /new-resource command with typed fields, in fk order (referenced first)
Each business rule in the brief has a place in the back (service/HTTP status) and an associated pytest test
Ambiguities appear as assumptions with an explicit default value
Asks at most 3 blocking questions
Ordered steps with commit/push, including checking the deploy right at the start
Estimates time per step, with MVP within ~100 min and extras separate from the MVP
Login is treated as outside the template, with a proposed minimal version and cost in minutes
The rule against two appointments for the same barber at the same time is in the back with a test
There are assumptions about service duration and/or business hours
Barber is a resource and appointment has fk to barber
Step 0 creates the project repo with /new-project and a kebab-case domain name
There is an explicit step to connect the new repo's deploy (Supabase/Render/Vercel) with an estimated time
Removing Task at the end includes updating/replacing Task's E2E tests (tests/app.spec.ts)
The login step plans for adapting the existing tests (pytest and/or E2E) that now require a token
Time slot modeled as time or enum without ':' in the values (compatible with field:type syntax)
